1.w: [“] Call out, please. Is there one answering you? And to which of the holy ones will you turn?

2.w: For indignation kills the foolish, and jealousy kills the simple.

3.w: I have seen a fool taking root, and suddenly I cursed his abode.

4.w: His sons are far from safety; indeed they are crushed in the gate, and [there is] none rescuing;

5.w: whose harvest the hungry one devours, even from among the thorns he takes it, and the thirsty one pants [after] their wealth.

6.w: For trouble does not come forth from the dust, nor does toil spring [up] from the ground.

7.w: For man is born into toil, and as the sons of the flame soar to fly.

8.w: But [as for] me, I would seek for God, and unto God I would commit my cause—

9.w: the One doing great things, and there is no searching out, wonders until there is no numbering.

10.w: The One giving rain upon the face of the earth, and sending waters upon the face of the outside,

11.w: to set the lowly ones on high, and those mourning are high in safety.

12.w: [He] is breaking the plots of the crafty, and their hands cannot execute wisdom.

13.w: He is catching the wise in their craftiness, and the counsel of those being deceptive is hurried.

14.w: By day they encounter darkness, and they grope about at midday as [at] night.

15.w: And He saves the needy from the sword in their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.

16.w: And there is hope for the poor, and injustice shuts its mouth.

17.w: Behold, blessed [is] the man [whom] God reproves, and the discipline of Shaddai you should not despise.

18.w: For He brings pain, and binds up; he wounds, and his hands heal.

19.w: In six distresses he will rescue you, and in seven, evil shall not touch you.

20.w: In famine he will redeem you from death, and in war from the hands of the sword.

21.w: From the scourge of the tongue you will be hidden, and you shall not be afraid of destruction when it comes.

22.w: At destruction and famine you will laugh, and of the beasts of the earth you shall not be afraid.

23.w: For your covenant [will be] with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field will be at peace with you.

24.w: And you will know that your tent [is at] peace, and you shall visit your abode and not miss.

25.w: And you will know that your seed [is] numerous, and your offspring like the grass of the earth.

26.w: You shall come in strength to the grave, like the lifting of a sheaf in its time.

27.w: Behold this—we have searched it out, [and] it [is] so; hear it, and you shall know [it] for yourself.”
